summary.summary: PARTIAL on brackets for the clumping onset of the six-axis gas with vacancies. BELOW: the seven-state single-site conditional has two channels that move oppositely in the fugacity - at uniform weights only occupancy couples and the Dobrushin coefficient FALLS with z, away from uniform the content channel dominates and it RISES - so a sup over a grid of z proves nothing; instead, because the five unchanged neighbours contribute the same factor to both weights and cancel, the single-neighbour weight ratio is independent of them AND of z, giving the z-free bound (M-m)/(M+m) and hence uniqueness AT EVERY FUGACITY wherever 6(M-m)/(M+m) < 1 - certified here for (1,1,1) and (9,8,8) up to c/c_0 = 5/4. CONTENT-LESS: with p = q = r the law is exactly the lattice gas of bond activity c*w, at the neutral scale c_0 w = 1 and the Dobrushin coefficient is identically 0, so the sites are independent and there is no transition at any fugacity; the onset for c > c_0 is the Z^3 Ising transition at c/c_0 = exp(4 K_c) = 2.4269..., which is literature and calibrates the bound above as lossy by about a factor two. ABOVE: the chessboard tool is available exactly on c >= c_0, p >= q, p + q >= 2r - the last two scale-free and omitted from the unit's statement - but the contour count is NOT done, so part (a) yields the region where the method applies and no theorem

what: DERIVATION, independent attempt 1 of 4: Brackets for where moving records clump. SETTING (the owner's working reading, 2026-09-20; block 39, the open PR titled 'ail39: records that move'): a site is empty or carries ONE record; a record carries its content (six axes); two neighbouring records weigh W = c * omega, omega = p, q, r for equal, opposite, orthogonal axes; a bond with an empty end weighs 1; the axioms' rule K (normalized over contents) does not depend on the scale c. MOTION: a record chooses between its position and an empty neighbouring position in proportion to the pair weights it would have there; this is in detailed balance with the static law on the occupied set. The neutral scale c_0 = 6/(p + q + 4r): an empty neighbour weighs what a record of random content weighs on average, and it is the least scale at which the law with vacancies is reflection positive through bond planes. Simulator: probes/lib/moving_gas.py p q r scale rho L sweeps seed (scale = a number or the word neutral). TASK: rigorous brackets for the onset of clumping of the six-axis gas with vacancies (the static law on the occupied set with a fugacity z per record; clumping = two translation-invariant states of different density at one fugacity). (a) ABOVE: for c p large a contour argument between a dense aligned state and the empty state; the reflection positivity of block 39's T5 (valid for c >= c_0, p >= q, p + q >= 2r) makes the chessboard estimate available: give an explicit region of (c, p, q, r). (b) BELOW: a uniqueness region for every fugacity (a one-site criterion in the enlarged one-site space of seven states). (c) For content-less records reduce to the known two-valued model and state what is proved and what is literature. Exact finite checks of every inequality used. DELIVERABLE, in your unit worktree on ai/probes: probes/work/derive/moving-clumping-bounds/<your worker name>/ATTEMPT.md and check.py. ATTEMPT.md: (1) the exact statement you attempt; (2) numbered steps, each marked PROVED (argument given in full), CHECKED (a finite fact check.py verifies exactly) or ASSUMED; (3) if the route fails, the FIRST step that fails and why: a precise no-go for a route is a result; (4) what would finish it. check.py: exact arithmetic (fractions, integers, sympy) for every finite claim; it prints `SUMMARY: PROVED ...`, `SUMMARY: COUNTEREXAMPLE ...`, `SUMMARY: PARTIAL <what is new and exact>` or `SUMMARY: ROUTE FAILS AT <step>`, and a line `HIT: <the claim>` ONLY when you claim a proof, a counterexample, or a new exact partial result others can build on; a HIT is handed to a worker of another model family to referee line by line, so write for a hostile reader. Rules: definitions come from the notes on the PR branches named above (git fetch origin <branch>; git show origin/<branch>:<note>; find them with gh pr view <n> --json files,headRefName); any outside theorem you use must be re-proved at the scope you use it or listed under ASSUMED; no status words (proved theorems are promoted by the supervisor after the referee). Have your own plan BEFORE reading the prior attempts printed at claim time; then either build on a refereed partial result or take a different route.
